package_info.why_malicious: The report does not describe a malicious package or embedded malicious code. Instead, it highlights a security risk due to the default configuration of anonymous read access in Nexus Repository, which can be exploited by attackers to exfiltrate or access sensitive artifacts. This is a misconfiguration risk, not a case of malware.

behavioral_signatures: Anonymous (unauthenticated) download requests to the Nexus Repository, especially for sensitive or private artifacts.
Unusual volume or frequency of anonymous access to repository endpoints.
Access logs showing artifact downloads from IPs or geographies not associated with legitimate users.
file_indicators: Nexus Repository configuration files with 'anonymous' user enabled for read/download permissions (e.g., security.xml, realm.properties).
network_indicators: HTTP GET requests to /repository/* endpoints without authentication headers.
Repeated access to artifact download URLs from unknown or external IP addresses.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Audit Nexus Repository configuration for enabled anonymous read/download access. Monitor access logs for unauthenticated download requests, especially for sensitive or private artifacts. Set up alerts for unusual patterns of anonymous access, such as high-frequency downloads or access from unexpected IP addresses. Regularly review and restrict anonymous permissions to minimize exposure.
